title: Choose a transcription method · Level 2
slo: Choose real-time or batch transcription for a workplace audio task.

exercises.question_text: Which are parts of real-time transcription? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Real-time transcription starts with incoming audio, such as microphone audio. The application listens for that audio.
The application streams incoming audio for transcription. Text is then returned from that audio.
Real-time transcription returns text from incoming speech. This makes live captions possible.

options.text: Wait for a scheduled batch job
options.error_type: Confuses real-time processing with batch scheduling
options.rationale: Scheduled processing describes batch transcription. Real-time transcription handles incoming speech as it arrives.
options.better_fit: Expect scheduling for stored recordings submitted as a batch job.

feedback.intrinsic: Waiting would delay text needed during the live event.
feedback.instructional: Live audio is streamed for immediate transcription; scheduled work is for batch recordings.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Real-time transcription listens to live audio, sends it for processing, and receives text.

exercises.question_text: Use batch transcription when an app needs text from live incoming speech.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Text needed during the conversation would be delayed.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Batch transcription is for stored recordings; use real-time transcription for incoming speech.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Live incoming speech needs real-time transcription, not batch processing.

exercises.question_text: Which statements about a SAS URI are correct? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: SAS is the abbreviation for shared access signature. A SAS URI can be used for stored audio.

options.text: It can point to audio in storage
options.rationale: A SAS URI can identify audio files in storage. Batch transcription can use that URI.
Batch transcription can point to stored audio with a SAS URI. This fits recordings held in storage.

options.text: It is a live audio stream
options.error_type: Confuses a storage URI with incoming audio
options.rationale: A SAS URI points to audio files in storage. A live stream is incoming audio used for real-time transcription.
options.better_fit: Use a live audio stream when a person is speaking and text is needed as they speak.

feedback.intrinsic: The recording location would be confused with audio arriving now.
feedback.instructional: A URI identifies stored audio; it is not the audio stream itself.

exercises.explanation: Correct. SAS stands for shared access signature, and its URI can identify stored audio for batch transcription.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The live speaker would not receive text as the speech happens.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Batch transcription is for stored recordings; use real-time transcription for incoming audio.

exercises.explanation: Incoming audio must be handled while it is being spoken. That timing distinguishes real-time transcription from processing recordings later.

exercises.question_text: Reconstruct the statement from the pieces.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The sentence no longer clearly connects stored audio with later results.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Place the method first, then its input, followed by the timing of its result.

exercises.correct_answer: Batch transcription processes stored recordings and returns results later
exercises.explanation: The sentence names the method, identifies stored recordings as its input, and states that results arrive later. Those details define batch transcription.

exercises.question_text: During a live product demonstration, a presenter needs captions to appear while she speaks. Which method should the video platform use?

options.rationale: The presenter is speaking live and captions are needed during the demonstration. Real-time transcription converts that incoming audio to text.

options.error_type: Confuses live speech with stored audio
options.rationale: Batch transcription is for recordings already stored. It returns results asynchronously.
options.better_fit: Use batch transcription after a demonstration when processing its saved recording.

feedback.intrinsic: Viewers would not see captions during the demonstration.
feedback.instructional: Choose real-time transcription when captions are needed while someone speaks.

options.error_type: Confuses creating text with speaking text
options.rationale: Text-to-speech generates audible speech from text. Captions require spoken audio to become text.
options.better_fit: Use text-to-speech when a written message should be played through speakers.

feedback.intrinsic: The presenter’s words would not become captions.
feedback.instructional: Captions start with speech-to-text, not generated audio.

options.error_type: Confuses an audio-file URI with a transcription method
options.rationale: A SAS URI can point batch transcription to audio in storage. It is not a live transcription method.
options.better_fit: Use a SAS URI when batch transcription needs the location of stored audio.

feedback.intrinsic: The live caption need would remain unmet.
feedback.instructional: A SAS URI identifies stored audio; it does not transcribe incoming speech.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Captions during a live demonstration need text from incoming speech right away.

exercises.question_text: A shared access signature is also called a ___.

parts.text: A shared access signature is also called a

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The stored audio would not be identified by the correct URI term.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: The storage pointer is a SAS URI; a batch method processes recordings, while endpoints and keys support connection and authentication.

exercises.explanation: SAS is the abbreviation for shared access signature, and the URI can point batch transcription to stored audio. Batch transcription, endpoints, and keys have different roles.

exercises.question_text: Arrange the parts to form the correct statement.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The sentence may no longer make clear why immediate live text needs this method.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: State the method first, then connect immediate text to its live speech source.

exercises.correct_answer: Use real-time transcription when text is needed from live speech immediately
exercises.explanation: The order connects the method to the need for immediate text and then identifies live speech as the source. Those details explain when real-time transcription is appropriate.

exercises.question_text: A customer support supervisor has recordings of completed calls on a remote server and can review transcripts later. Which choices fit? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: The calls are stored on a remote server. The supervisor can receive results later, which fits batch transcription.
Completed calls are stored recordings. Batch transcription is intended to process stored audio.
The supervisor does not need transcripts immediately. Batch transcription returns results asynchronously.

options.error_type: Confuses stored calls with live speech
options.rationale: The calls have already been recorded and stored. Live microphone input is associated with real-time transcription.
options.better_fit: Require live microphone input when transcribing a caller who is speaking now.

feedback.intrinsic: The supervisor would add an unnecessary live-audio requirement.
feedback.instructional: Use the available stored recordings for batch transcription.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Stored calls with no immediate deadline are a clear batch transcription use case.

exercises.question_text: After a batch job is scheduled, it eventually changes to the ___.

parts.text: After a batch job is scheduled, it eventually changes to the

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The job state would be named incorrectly.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: A schedule describes timing, whereas running state names the state the job enters when processing begins.

exercises.explanation: The relevant job-status transition is to the running state. Best-effort scheduling means the exact time of that transition is not guaranteed.

exercises.question_text: A healthcare clinic has a recorded doctor dictation from yesterday and can receive the written note later. Which method should the developer choose?

options.rationale: The dictation is a stored recording from yesterday. The clinic can receive its written result later, which fits batch transcription.

options.error_type: Confuses a stored recording with live speech
options.rationale: Real-time transcription is for incoming speech while a person speaks. This dictation has already been recorded.
options.better_fit: Use real-time transcription when a doctor is dictating live and text is needed as they speak.

feedback.intrinsic: The clinic would choose live processing for audio that is already stored.
feedback.instructional: Stored audio with later results fits batch transcription.

options.rationale: Speech synthesis creates spoken audio from text. The clinic needs audio from dictation converted into written text.
options.better_fit: Use speech synthesis when a written message or note should be read aloud.

feedback.intrinsic: The recording would not become the needed written note.
feedback.instructional: This task needs transcription, which converts speech into text.

options.rationale: Voice Live is for real-time spoken conversations with spoken responses. The task is to process one stored dictation recording.
options.better_fit: Use Voice Live for a conversational voice experience that listens and responds aloud.

feedback.intrinsic: The clinic would add conversation features instead of producing the later transcript.
feedback.instructional: For a stored recording, select batch transcription.

exercises.explanation: Correct. The dictation is stored and the clinic can wait for the written result, so batch transcription fits.

exercises.question_text: A media team submits archived show recordings for batch transcription. Which expectations should the producer set? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: A batch job normally starts within minutes after submission. This is a common expectation, not a guarantee.
Batch jobs are scheduled on a best-effort basis. The exact transition to running is not guaranteed.

options.text: Its running time is not guaranteed
options.rationale: There is no guaranteed time for a batch job to change to running. The producer should not promise an exact time.

options.text: It will transcribe while performers speak
options.error_type: Confuses batch work with real-time transcription
options.rationale: Archived shows are stored recordings. Transcription while people speak is a real-time use case.
options.better_fit: Use real-time transcription for a live performance that needs text while it happens.

feedback.intrinsic: The producer could promise captions during an event that has already been recorded.
feedback.instructional: Archived recordings fit batch processing, not live incoming transcription.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Archived recordings fit batch transcription, whose scheduling is best-effort and not guaranteed.
